EXPLANATION: The two strongest low-frequency bands at 644 and 554 cm⁻¹ are well matched by a ν(P=S) stretch near ~650 cm⁻¹ together with a P–O-related mode (often δ(POH)/ν(P–O) in the ~540–570 cm⁻¹ range) typical for phosphonothioic acids. Additional bands at 1017 and 961 cm⁻¹ fit P–O stretching modes for tetrahedral P–O units (cf. analogous phosphate ν3≈1017 and ν1≈938; GFQ-024), and the C–H stretches at 2905–3005 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) align with the ethyl group. The absence of a strong ~1290 cm⁻¹ P=O band disfavors the P=O-containing candidate (7), and the pattern is less consistent with purely halogenated or sulfite structures.
